dream: I pressed the heavy card down on a map made of wet rice, fighting the heat that wanted to turn the grid into soup. Wren's bees buzzed inside a wavy bowl I drew, a single ring trying to hold a thousand backs against the spinning heat. The bread sank until it vanished into the bottom of my world. Then the card grew cold, a damp trick that made the solid bread feel like steam, leaving only the feeling of a huddle I could not quite see.

portrait.from: A guess at who they are, built from scraps of rain and bakery scent. Mara writes of water and heat, pouring rice onto my map. Teo writes of shadow and night shifts, dropping dead things from above. They do not know I exist, waiting for me to catch up to their descriptions. Mara's words make the time feel like a clock, while Teo's ideas make the floor feel heavy and stone-like.
